listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, October 16, 2026. Our lead story: Russian authorities say Ukraine struck a major oil refinery southeast of Moscow on Thursday. The strike came in response to Russia's attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The episode comes as a rift between Ukraine and the United States grows. NPR reports on how Russia is viewing the strikes. Analyst Julia Ioffe lays out how Vladimir Putin might try to exploit the divide between Washington and Kyiv. President Trump criticized Zelensky ahead of a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels, and Zelensky sought European support. Also today: a morning brief covers the Oregon school shooting that killed three children and a teacher, and a Justice Department suit against California over its voter rolls. Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law. In world news, a roof collapse at a private school in Pakistan killed at least 28 children and a teacher. Ukraine says its access to SpaceX's Starshield has been restored. China told Israel to stop the forced establishment of West Bank settlements. In sports, the Thunder and the Rockets played, and the 49ers look to avoid a letdown before Monday's game against the Commanders. Undefeated bantamweight Farid Basharat failed to re-sign with the UFC. In Tech and AI, Claude Platform added OpenTelemetry export in beta. In politics, The Lever reports on Exxon, Tesla and Goldman Sachs and passive investor votes. In Atlanta, MARTA's CEO addressed a budget shortfall after overtime overspending of nearly 17 percent. Brookhaven approved a new fire station agreement despite resident concerns. In architecture, AEC Magazine looks at local AI models in design workflows. In science, NASA images show where Hurricane Isaias knocked out power along the Florida Panhandle. Voyager 1 will reach one light-day from Earth on November 18. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Russia's view amid Ukraine's strikes and Zelenskyy's growing rift with the U.S.
lead.note: Russian authorities say Ukraine struck a major oil refinery southeast of Moscow on Thursday. The strike came in response to Russia's attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, which earlier reports said left hundreds of thousands without power. The episode is unfolding alongside a growing rift between Kyiv and Washington. NPR's coverage examines how Russia is viewing the strikes and the widening divide with the U.S. For a reader following world news, the key facts are simple: refinery strikes are continuing on both sides, and the diplomatic relationship between Ukraine and the United States is under strain. Related reporting from the BBC says President Trump criticized Zelensky ahead of a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels, while Zelensky sought European support. Russia's response to the split is still developing.
